note:
2014 Panini Prizm FIFA World Cup, acquired from TCDB 2026-09-13 (Beckett is offline for
maintenance since 2026-09-09, so the queue's beckett-xlsx lane could not be used).
136 sub-checklists: the 201-card base set, 13 base parallel rungs and 11 insert families
with their own rungs. Every rung paginated to exhaustion (TCDB pages at 100 rows; a
single-page read clipped the base set at 100 of 201).

SETKEY — `panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup`, per Drew's ruling 2026-09-13: the 2014 FIFA World
Cup release is its OWN product key, like the 2025 FIFA release. NO src change was needed —
the key already exists and is already a normalizeSetKey FIXED POINT. Verified by running
the function rather than reading the table:

  normalizeSetKey('2014 Panini Prizm FIFA World Cup') === 'panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup'
  normalizeSetKey('panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup')      === 'panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup'

setkey-reconciliation.json already rules the key verdict `distinct`, canonical itself, on
96,562 checklist rows, with the rule 'product-family collapse — `panini-prizm` is an
ancestor of `panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup`, and product-family collapse is forbidden (Drew
2026-09-03)'. reconcileSetKey returns final:true, so the key short-circuits ahead of the
unanchored /panini-prizm/ pattern that would otherwise swallow the qualifier.

COMPETITION-NAMED, NOT YEAR-SCOPED — the same shape as its siblings
`panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup-qatar` (2022) and `panini-prizm-fifa-club-world-cup`. The
year-scoped PRIZM_FIFA_YEARS mechanism exists for the BARE title 'Panini Prizm' in soccer,
which is genuinely ambiguous and needs the (sport, year) cell to disambiguate. This
product's own name states the competition, so it needs no sport/year scoping and none was
added.

The rows already on this key are ALL 2026 (reconciliation evidence years '2026-2026'), so
these 2014 rows land in their own (sport, year) cell under the same product and collide
with nothing. The pool's 2,974 soccer/2014 sales sit on `panini-prizm` and are expected to
fold here through the rematch once this checklist is ingested.

isAuto and printRun are read from TCDB's own row attributes (AU, SN<n>), not inferred:
the Signatures and Combo Signatures rungs carry AU + SN10 and are written as autos /10.
parallel is BLANK for a plain rung — blank means unknown, never 'Base'.
The rung name is what the rung ADDS to the anchor ('Gold Prizm'), per the one-format rule.
